# Gx Protocol Analyzer - Technical Specification

## 1. Project Overview

### 1.1 Purpose
The Gx Protocol Analyzer is a sophisticated network analysis tool designed to capture, decode, and analyze Gx interface communications between mobile core network elements.

### 1.2 Key Objectives
- Real-time packet capture and decoding
- Protocol-specific message parsing
- Comprehensive statistical analysis
- Configurable filtering and reporting
- High-performance, scalable architecture

## 2. System Architecture

### 2.1 Component Structure
1. Network Capture Layer
2. Protocol Decoder
3. Analysis Engine
4. Reporting and Visualization Module
5. Configuration Management

### 2.2 Technology Stack
- Language: Rust (for performance and memory safety)
- Networking: libpcap
- Parsing: Nom parsing library
- Database: InfluxDB (time-series metrics)
- Visualization: Grafana
- Frontend: Tauri (Rust + Web Technologies)

## 3. Detailed Component Specifications

### 3.1 Network Capture Layer
- Support for multiple network interfaces
- Raw packet capture with zero-copy techniques
- DPDK integration for high-performance capture
- Support for:
  - Physical interfaces
  - Virtual interfaces
  - PCAP file input

#### Interface Definition
```rust
trait NetworkCaptureInterface {
    fn start_capture(&self) -> Result<(), CaptureError>;
    fn stop_capture(&self) -> Result<(), CaptureError>;
    fn get_packet_stream(&self) -> PacketStream;
}
```

### 3.2 Protocol Decoder
- Comprehensive Gx protocol message parsing
- Support for all Gx message types:
  - Diameter Credit Control Application (DCCA)
  - Charging Rule Installation
  - Session Establishment
  - Policy and Charging Control (PCC)

#### Parsing Strategy
- Nom-based zero-copy parsing
- Detailed message structure extraction
- Performance-optimized decoding

### 3.3 Analysis Engine
- Real-time message correlation
- Statistical aggregation
- Anomaly detection
- Performance metrics tracking

#### Key Analysis Metrics
- Message rate
- Latency distribution
- Error rates
- Session establishment times
- Diameter result codes

### 3.4 Reporting Module
- Time-series metrics storage
- Configurable dashboards
- Export capabilities
- Alerting mechanisms

### 3.5 Configuration Management
- Dynamic interface configuration
- Filter rule management
- Capture session settings

## 4. Performance Requirements

### 4.1 Performance Targets
- Capture: 10 Gbps sustained
- Decode: <1ms per packet
- Storage: Compressed time-series storage
- Minimal CPU overhead (<10% on standard server)

### 4.2 Scalability
- Horizontal scaling support
- Distributed capture capabilities
- Clustered analysis mode

## 5. Security Considerations
- Encrypted configuration storage
- Role-based access control
- Secure packet data handling
- Compliance with telecom security standards

## 6. Deployment Options
- Standalone executable
- Docker container
- Kubernetes deployment
- Cloud-native architecture support

## 7. Development Milestones
1. Network capture prototype
2. Basic protocol decoder
3. Analysis engine development
4. Reporting module
5. Configuration management
6. Performance optimization
7. Extended testing and validation

## 8. Testing Strategy
- Unit testing for each component
- Integration testing
- Performance benchmark testing
- Fault injection testing
- Compliance testing with 3GPP standards

## 9. Future Extensibility
- Support for additional diameter interfaces
- Machine learning-based anomaly detection
- Enhanced visualization capabilities

## 10. Open Source Considerations
- MIT License
- Clear contribution guidelines
- Comprehensive documentation

---

Estimated Development Time: 4-6 months
Estimated Team Size: 3-5 senior engineers
